rounds.text: Orchasp Ltd trades at a steep discount to its asset backing with a price-to-book ratio of 0.45x, as the share price sits at ₹ 1.59 against a book value of ₹ 3.52 [E2]. This asset discount becomes even starker when compared against the broader sector benchmark price-to-book ratio of 7.28x [E7]. The business has demonstrated an acceleration in top-line expansion over medium-term horizons, achieving a compounded sales growth rate of 21% over the last 5 years [E15]. Operational efficiency is also showing tentative signs of structural improvement, with the operating margin recovering by 2 percentage points to -13% in March 2026 compared to three years prior [E30]. Furthermore, the company exhibits a positive return on assets of 0.45%, standing in stark contrast to the deeply negative sector benchmark of -40.7% [E8]. Conceded: [E31].

The bull highlights a low price-to-book ratio of 0.45x [E2], but this discount is entirely justified by a severe collapse in near-term fundamentals, evidenced by quarterly operating margins plunging to -253% in March 2026, a catastrophic drop of 296 percentage points year-over-year [E31]. While the bull points to a 5-year compounded sales growth of 21% [E15], this historical metric masks a severe growth stall and subsequent decay, as 3-year compounded sales growth is -3% [E16] and trailing twelve-month growth has slowed to a negligible 1% [E17], compounded by a brutal 77% year-over-year quarterly sales collapse [E70]. The bull’s reliance on a 2-percentage-point multi-year margin recovery to -13% [E30] is deeply misleading when the company continues to operate at a negative margin and suffers from explicitly flagged decelerating earnings growth [E71]. Conceded: [E7, E8]. Furthermore, valuing the company on its asset book value ignores the reality of a stock pinned near the absolute bottom of its annual range at just 4% of its 52-week spread [E5], commanding a rich P/E of 52.5x [E1] despite offering zero dividend yield [E4].
